SUPPLY PROCEDURE: FOOD RATIONING UNDER SHORTFALL

Overview
A confirmed shortfall in food stock relative to the resupply window requires an
immediate rationing plan. This procedure governs how the crew's daily caloric
intake is adjusted until the resupply vehicle arrives.

Rationing Sequence
1. Confirm the current food energy stock on hand and the days remaining until
   the next scheduled resupply arrival.
2. Set the daily per-person ration at the highest level that leaves a
   non-negative projected buffer at resupply, rounding down to the nearest
   10 kcal.
3. Suspend high-exertion spacewalks and heavy maintenance tasks to reduce
   metabolic burn while rationing is in effect.
4. Prioritize protein and micronutrient rations over caloric bulk to preserve
   crew health and function at a reduced caloric intake.

Escalation
Step 1: If the projected buffer is negative at any ration level within the
allowed range, escalate to mission control and request an expedited resupply.
Step 2: Log the rationing decision and the modeled survival probability in the
mission log for post-event review.

Follow-Up Checks
- Recheck the projected buffer daily as consumption and stock levels are confirmed.
- Confirm crew health markers remain stable throughout the rationing period.
